children: Shares of Laurus Labs surged 3.81 per cent to ₹2,329.60 on the NSE by 10.15 AM on Friday, touching a fresh 52-week high of ₹2,343 in early trade, a day after the pharma and CDMO company reported sharply higher earnings for the July–September quarter. The stock has gained over 139 per cent in the past year and is up 109 per cent year-to-date, significantly outpacing its benchmark index NIFTY MIDCAP 50.

Motilal Oswal, in a note dated October 30, maintained a Buy rating on the stock with a revised target price of ₹2,830, implying an upside of about 26 per cent from the previous close of ₹2,244. The brokerage raised its earnings estimates by 28 per cent and 30 per cent for FY27 and FY28 respectively, citing the scale-up of the CDMO segment, including peptide manufacturing, a steady rise in affordable medicine supply, and a better segmental mix. The firm noted that EBITDA and PAT beat its own estimates by 22 per cent and 38 per cent, calling out favourable segmental mix and currency benefits as key margin drivers.

For the second quarter of FY27, Laurus Labs reported consolidated net revenue of ₹2,206 crore, up 33 per cent year-on-year from ₹1,653 crore. EBITDA came in at ₹750 crore against ₹403 crore a year ago, with margins expanding to 34 per cent from 24.4 per cent. Net profit nearly tripled to ₹436 crore from ₹194 crore in the same period last year.

The growth was driven primarily by the CDMO small molecules segment, which rose 86 per cent year-on-year. The company also announced the proposed acquisition of a 60 per cent stake in Canada-based Galenvs Sciences to strengthen its oligonucleotide capabilities, and a 52 per cent stake in Hyderabad-based SI & C Resins to support peptide manufacturing.
Trading volume on the NSE stood at 29.41 lakh shares with a turnover of ₹679 crore by mid-morning, reflecting strong investor interest.

title: Laurus Labs hits 52-week high as strong Q2 results fuel buying
